numerical_failure.observed_behavior: On native complex arrays with a NaN component, the fastpath viewed complex arrays as float pairs and compared real and imaginary parts independently, so array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj])) returned False with dtype_equal=True, and Series.equals returned False, although both elements are NA.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Two elements that are both NA are equivalent even when their non-NaN parts differ, so array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj])) should return True, matching the dtype_equal=False path and the 3.0.x behaviour; Series.equals should return True.
trigger_conditions: native complex dtype (complex128 or complex64) arrays
an element with a NaN real or imaginary part in both arrays
non-NaN parts of the paired elements differ
dtype_equal=True path using the float-pair fastpath
oracle_clues: dtype_equal=True and dtype_equal=False paths must agree
Series.equals should return True for both-NA elements

numerical_characteristics.dtype: complex128 and complex64 (native), plus byte-swapped >c16 and >c8 in the regression test
category_specific_evidence: NaN enters through the real or imaginary part of a complex element; the correct behaviour is whole-element NA, so an element is NA if either part is NaN and two NA elements are equivalent even when their non-NaN parts differ.
The old fastpath viewed native complex arrays as float pairs and compared real and imaginary parts independently, which is the wrong handling of NaN.
Reported example: array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj])) gave dtype_equal=True -> False but dtype_equal=False -> True, and Series.equals returned False where it should return True.
Pre-fix 3.0.x used np.isnan on the complex array and returned True for this case.
The fix routes all complex through the numpy comparison ((left == right) | (np.isnan(left) & np.isnan(right))).all(), which uses whole-element isna.

test_array_equivalent_complex_nan_component is parametrized over dtype_equal in [True, False] and dtype in [c16, c8, >c16, >c8]; it covers NaN in the real part, NaN in the imaginary part, a genuine NA mixed with an equal finite element, and differing finite elements that must not be equivalent.
No inf, -inf, signed-zero or subnormal values are mentioned in any passage.
reproduction_risks: Use an element with a NaN in only one component (for example 1+nanj vs 2+nanj) rather than a fully finite complex value, since only the NaN-component case exercises the bug.
Compare both dtype_equal=True and dtype_equal=False; the bug is their disagreement.
Include byte-swapped complex (>c16, >c8), because the fix also covers non-native complex and the pre-fix code had a native-check path for it.
No tolerance applies: the checks are exact boolean equivalence, not approximate comparison.
